 New Micro-Moth Species Discovered in Assam 
 Star marking (1-5) indicates the importance of topic -->
 Why in News?   
 A new micro-moth species, Glyphipterix brevimucronata , has been discovered near Hollongapar Gibbon Sanctuary in Jorhat district of Assam, marking the first taxonomic addition to India's sedge moth family in nearly a century.   
 Key Points   
 Physical Features: It has a wingspan of approximately 6.5 mm, with brown forewings, a yellowish metallic sheen and distinctive white markings.   
 Research Publication: The discovery was reported by Kishore Chandra Sahoo of ICAR-Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI), Assam, in the international journal Zootaxa .   
 Read more : Hollongapar Gibbon Sanctuary

 Assam Approves ₹15 Crore for First Phase of Zubeen Kshetra 
 Star marking (1-5) indicates the importance of topic -->
 Why in News?   
 The Assam Government has sanctioned ₹15 crore for the first phase of the proposed Zubeen Kshetra at Sonapur , in memory of renowned Assamese singer Zubeen Garg , on his 54 th birth anniversary on 18 November 2026.   
 Key Points   
 Project Approval: Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma approved the first phase of work on Zubeen Kshetra.   
 Objective: Zubeen Kshetra aims to preserve and celebrate Zubeen Garg's contributions to music, art and culture and keep his legacy alive for future generations.   
 Zubeen Garg:    
 Zubeen Garg: Born Zubeen Borthakur on 18 November 1972 ; died on 19 September 2025 .   
 Debut Album: Anamika ( 1992 ).   
 First Recorded Songs: “Tumi Junu Pariba Hun” and “Tumi Junaki Hubakh” for the album Ritu ( 1993 ).   
 National Film Award: Won the Rajat Kamal for Best Music Direction for the non-feature film Echoes of Silence .    
 Won Best Playback Singer at the Global Indian Film Awards (GIFA) for the song “Ya Ali” in 2006.   
 Read More: Zubeen Garg

 Vadnagar Archaeological Museum Wins Red Dot: Best of the Best Award 2026 
 Star marking (1-5) indicates the importance of topic -->
 Why in News?   
 The Anant Anadi Vadnagar Archaeological Experiential Museum in Gujarat has won the prestigious Red Dot: Best of the Best Award 2026 in Berlin, Germany.   
 Key Points   
 Achievement: It is India's first and only museum to receive the Red Dot: Best of the Best Award.   
 Opening: The museum was opened to the public in February 2025 .   
 Historical Importance: Vadnagar is among India's oldest continuously inhabited fortified towns, with evidence of human habitation dating back to approximately 750–800 BCE .   
 Archaeological Excavations: The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) conducted excavations between 2016 and 2022 , uncovering evidence of seven cultural periods.   
 Historical Periods: The archaeological findings reflect the Mauryan, Indo-Greek, Shaka-Kshatrapa, Maitraka, Solanki, Sultanate and Mughal periods.   
 Religious Heritage: Excavations have revealed evidence of Hinduism, Buddhism and Jainism, including a Buddhist monastery and a structure believed to be an early stupa.   
 Archaeological Survey of India (ASI):   
 Ministry: Functions under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India .   
 Established: 1861 by Sir Alexander Cunningham .   
 Headquarters: New Delhi .   
 Statutory Status: After Independence, ASI was established as a statutory body under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958 (AMASR Act) .   
 Antiquities: Also regulates matters related to antiquities under the Antiquities and Art Treasures Act, 1972 .   
 Read More: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)

 Vaibhav Sooryavanshi Becomes Youngest Captain in Men's T20 Cricket History 
 Star marking (1-5) indicates the importance of topic -->
 Why in News?   
 Bihar cricketer Vaibhav Sooryavanshi , aged 15 years and 232 days , became the youngest captain in men's T20 cricket history after leading Bihar against Saurashtra in the 2026–27 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy at Holkar Stadium .   
 Key Points   
 Record: Sooryavanshi surpassed Croatia's Zach Vukusic , who had previously held the record after captaining his national side at the age of 17 years and 311 days.   
 Tournament: He led Bihar in its opening match of the 2026–27 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy against Saurashtra.   
 International Debut: He made his T20 International debut for India five months before this achievement.   
 Under-19 Cricket: He was part of India's Under-19 World Cup-winning campaign in Zimbabwe earlier in 2026.   
 ACC Rising Stars Tournament: He is set to join India A for the ACC Rising Stars Emerging Tournament in Doha, beginning on 19 November 2026.   
 T20 Achievement: In November 2025, he scored 144 runs off 42 balls for India A against the UAE in the ACC Rising Stars tournament.   
 Read More: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi

 MS Dhoni Retires from IPL 
 Star marking (1-5) indicates the importance of topic -->
 Why in News?   
 Former Indian cricket captain Mahendra Singh Dhoni announced his retirement from the Indian Premier League (IPL) as a player on 17 November 2026 . Chennai Super Kings (CSK) announced that he will take up the role of Team Mentor from the 2027 IPL season , bringing an end to his nearly two-decade-long playing association with the franchise.   
 Key Points:   
 Retirement Announcement: Chennai Super Kings officially announced Dhoni's transition from player to mentor.   
 Dhoni's IPL career began in 2008 , with the inaugural edition of the tournament.   
 He was part of CSK from its inception, except during the 2016 and 2017 seasons when the franchise was suspended.   
 Dhoni's IPL Career Statistics:   
 IPL Matches: 278.   
 Runs: 5,439.   
 Batting Average: 38.30.   
 IPL Titles as CSK Captain: Five.   
 He represented CSK for 17 seasons and Rising Pune Supergiant for two seasons.   
 Chennai Super Kings' Achievements under Dhoni: Dhoni led CSK to five IPL titles: 2010,2011,2018,2021 and 2023.   
 CSK also won the Champions League T20 twice under his captaincy, in 2010 and 2014.   
 Leadership and Contribution: Dhoni is popularly known as 'Captain Cool' because of his calm temperament and leadership.   
 He is renowned for his wicketkeeping, finishing ability and tactical understanding of the game.   
 He handed over CSK's captaincy to Ruturaj Gaikwad ahead of the 2024 season.   
 His experience will now be used to guide younger players and support the team's transition.   
 International Cricket Achievements:   
 ICC T20 World Cup: 2007.   
 ICC Cricket World Cup: 2011.   
 ICC Champions Trophy: 2013.   
 He became the first captain to win all three major ICC limited-overs men's trophies.   
 He announced his retirement from international cricket on 15 August 2020 .   
 Significance of the New Role: Dhoni's transition to mentor will allow CSK to retain his leadership and institutional experience.   
 His role is expected to support young cricketers, team strategy and the franchise's long-term development.   
 His association with CSK continues despite his retirement from professional IPL playing.
